notes: Method: downloaded the OLLS C.R.S. 2026 Title 24 HTML (22.3 MB), stripped to text and matched every source_language fragment of all 36 rows programmatically (whitespace-normalised, exact substring) — 36/36 statute fragments found verbatim in §§ 24-72-112, -203, -205, -306; the three non-statute fragments were matched verbatim against the Legislative Council Staff fee posting (raw HTML), the June 12, 2024 LCS memorandum PDF and the LCS 'Colorado Law Summary: CORA' PDF (LAST REVIEWED 09/18/2024). Currency: § 24-72-205 source note ends at SB 23-286 (2023); § 24-72-203 gained only (3)(d) in 2024 (SB 24-210, county clerks); SB25-077 veto (4/17/2025) and SB26-107 postponed-indefinitely (3/5/2026) confirmed by search. Municipal scope: § 24-72-202(6)(a)(I) 'public records' covers 'political subdivision of the state' and § 24-72-202(1.1) 'custodian' is generic, so all_public_bodies is right for every CORA row; § 24-72-306(1) municipal police recordings note verified. Judgment rows kept CONFIRMED but flagged for the human queue via their existing manual_verification: dup.color.rate (color not distinguished in law), labor.review.rate (CORA names only 'research and retrieval'; $41.37 is an upper bound under either reading, chargeability itself is a legal judgment), rules.deposit.threshold (defers_to_city rests on § 205(6)(a)'s express delegation of R&R conditions to the custodian's published policy plus § 205(7)'s recognition of deposits — verifier considered 'silent' and found the delegation express enough), payment.depositClock ('no clock while unpaid' is an implication, flagged). Minor: rows 16 and 23 list source_type 'Statute; Official Guidance' though their only quoted language is guidance — harmless for a silent resolution. No rows corrected, refuted, or unverifiable; no new research beyond what the checks required.
